description:
This Salt & Straw ice cream has gone right in to our "Top 10 best ice creams", we'll be adding more to the Top 10 so keep an eye out ;)

It's such a mouthful to say but my word, it is worth saying. 

So what will you need to make this?

Ice Cream Ingredients:
100g Sugar
2 Tbsp Milk Powder
½ Tsp Salt
¼ Tsp Xanthan Gum
320ml Whole Milk
2 Tbsp Light Corn Syrup (Glucose in UK)
1 Tsp Molasses (Black Treacle in UK)
320ml Heavy (Double) Cream
2 Tsp Vanilla Extract

Cookie Dough:
60g Unsalted Butter at room temperature
2 Tbsp Sugar
55g Brown Sugar or Muscovardo Sugar
1 Tsp Salt
2 Tbsp Heavy (Double) Cream
1 Tsp Molasses
1 Tbsp Corn Syrup (Golden Syrup in UK)
1 Tsp Vanilla Extract
60g All-purpose Flour (Plain in UK) baked at 350°F (180°C) for 10 minutes
2 Tbsp Malt Powder
45g Semi-sweet Chocolate chips

Malted Fudge:
1 Tbsp Cold Water
2 Tsp Malt Powder
110g Corn Syrup
120ml Heavy Cream
1 Tbsp Unsalted Butter
⅛ Tsp Kosher Salt
1 Tbsp Cocoa Powder
85g of 80% Chocolate chopped

comments.author: @sj460162

comments.text:
Hi Steve,
You are correct if you look on a pint label, these recipes are for making at home using home machines. Tyler Malek from Salt & Straw created this version and posted it to Tasty almost 3 years ago now so people like you and I can make it at home. There are many ways to emulsify a recipe but in a base like this additional emulsifyers are simply not required. Give it a try, you won't be dissapointed. 
If you don't want to use xanthan gum, you can sub it for gelatin or your chosen stabiliser of choice. To be honest, you can leave it out completely and it won't effect the result too much. 
Let me know what you think if you do make it as it's one of our favourites.

Hi Steve, it’s an amazing combo isn’t it. As for the fat lumps, I’m going to ask what machine you’re using and how long did the churn take? 
Myself and some good friends and pro ice cream makers can only put it down to ingredients and churn speed/ time. Over churning can produce lumps of fat so that might be what’s happened for you. It could also be too high fat but I’ve made ice cream at 25% fat content and had no issues at all.
